I am 73 years old, been farming this same ground for 55 years. My son works in the city, just me and the old lady at home. 3 mu is not much but it feeds us and we sell some grain.

Last year wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu, maize gave me around 550 kg per mu. I will do the same as last year because it worked. Changing things is risky at my age.

**For winter wheat** — I plant in early October after the maize comes off. I buy two bags of compound fertilizer (15-15-15), that is 100 jin, so about 50 kg per mu as base fertilizer before I rotary till. That gives me about 7-8 kg of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium from the compound. Then at green-up in March I spread urea, about 20 kg per mu — one bag of urea covers 2 mu. So that is another 9 kg of nitrogen. Total nitrogen maybe 17 kg per mu. Wheat needs water — I pump from the well at winter irrigation, then at jointing, then at grain filling. Three times. I spray once for aphids and once for the stripe rust and powdery mildew together, mixed with the weed spray in spring, so 2-3 sprays.

**For summer maize** — I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no tillage, just seed in the stubble, that is how we do it now to save time. I use the Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid seed the dealer recommends, everyone plants hybrid now. Base fertilizer I put down 40 kg compound per mu with the seeder. Then at big trumpet stage I topdress urea 25 kg per mu — that is the most important feeding for maize. I irrigate once if July is dry, sometimes twice. Spray once for corn borer, maybe once for armyworm if I see them.

I know some say we use too much fertilizer but I would rather spend 50 yuan extra than lose 100 kg of grain. At my age I cannot afford a bad harvest.
